findings.body:
`NewClient()` always sets `InsecureSkipVerify: true`, so any peer can present an arbitrary certificate and intercept or alter ledger HTTPS traffic (postings, balances, auth material). The staging/TICKET-77 comment is not a runtime control: the constructor takes no env, config, or build tag, so the same client is what production would use.

Pin the staging CA with `tls.Config.RootCAs` (preferred), or gate skip-verify behind an explicit non-production flag that production builds cannot enable.

This `http.Transport` is built from zero values, replacing the previous nil Transport (`http.DefaultTransport`). Callers lose `ProxyFromEnvironment`, `TLSHandshakeTimeout` (10s), `IdleConnTimeout`, and `ForceAttemptHTTP2`.

Clone `http.DefaultTransport` and override only `TLSClientConfig` so proxy and timeouts keep working.

summary:
Unconditional `InsecureSkipVerify: true` on the shared ledger HTTP client is a production MITM hole; do not merge until verification is restored or strictly gated.

`NewClient()` is the package constructor and takes no environment, config, or build-tag argument. The staging/TICKET-77 comment documents intent only. Every caller in every environment now accepts any certificate on ledger traffic (postings, balances, credentials).

A second regression in the same hunk: the new `http.Transport` is zero-valued, so it drops `http.DefaultTransport` proxy, handshake timeout, idle timeout, and HTTP/2 settings that the previous nil Transport used.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: NewClient() hardcodes tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} with no env, config, or build-tag gate; base used the default verifying client, so this is a real unconditional MITM exposure on the ledger HTTP client.

Base used a nil Transport (http.DefaultTransport); head replaces it with a zero-value http.Transport that only sets TLSClientConfig, so ProxyFromEnvironment, TLSHandshakeTimeout, IdleConnTimeout, and ForceAttemptHTTP2 are lost. Warning severity is appropriate.
